A GitLab CI/CD conundrum!

To bypass a failed GitLab CI job and mark it as passed, you can use the `always_allow_failure` parameter. Here's how:

1. In your `.gitlab-ci.yml` file, update the relevant job to include this line:
```yaml
job:
  allow_failure: always
```
This will mark the job as successful even if it fails (i.e., returns a non-zero exit code).

Alternatively, you can also use the `when: never` parameter in combination with `allow_failure: always`. This way, the job will only run when there are changes to the pipeline's inputs:
```yaml
job:
  allow_failure: always
  when: never
```
By doing so, the job will still be considered successful, but its output won't affect the overall pipeline status.

Note that these solutions assume you want to keep the results of the failed job. If you don't care about the output and just want to mark it as passed, you can use `always_allow_failure` alone.

Hope this helps!
